newsitem.title: ROMANIA: SIX ROMANIAN BANKS BUY FRESH THREE-MONTH T-BILLS.
newsitem.headline: SIX ROMANIAN BANKS BUY FRESH THREE-MONTH T-BILLS.

text.p: Six Romanian banks have bought 380 billion lei from an issue of 1.0 trillion 91-day treasury bills offered by the Finance Ministry, keen to cover a bulging 1996 state budget deficit, official data showed on Friday.
The new T-bills, offered with a coupon giving an annual yield of 51.35 percent, mature on January 10, 1997.

Money market traders suggested on Thursday that recent rises of the central bank's one-week refinancing funds might seek to encourage banks to buy T-bills to help finance growing state budget deficits.

Banca Romana de Comert Exterior Bancorex SA, Banca Romana pentru Dezvoltare SA, Banca Comerciala Romana SA, Banc Post SA, Banca Agricola SA and MISR Romanian Bank bought the Finance Ministry papers on Friday.
The central bank has raised its one-week funds offer to 1.045 trillion lei this week from 940 billion last week and a previus 700 billion.
January-August budget showed a deficit of 1.9 trillion lei, while the forecast for the whole year is 4.27 trillion.

The remaining bills will be offered in two public subscription sessions on October 18 and 25. Their annual yield will equal the three-month Bucharest Interbank Bid Rate (BUBID) set five working days ahead of the session.
Three-month BUBID was 50.23 percent on Friday. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
